title: Telling time to the minute (age 7+)
keyIdea: Every small mark on the clock is one minute. Read times like 3:17 and 5:42 — minutes past before half past, and minutes to the next hour after half past — and match the digital form.
familyTip: Point to a wall clock and ask for the exact minute, not only 'about quarter past'. Say a digital time like 4:23 and have your child set the long hand.

visual.caption: Minute-time idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: every time must land on a big number

lab.caption: Flagship lab: count minute marks, set 3:17 and 4:23, read minutes to (5:42), match digital 2:09, catch multiples-of-5-only myth.

kid: Between the big numbers are small marks. Each small mark is one minute.
3:17 means 17 minutes past 3 — the long hand is not only on big numbers.
After half past you can say minutes to the next hour: 5:42 is 18 minutes to 6.
A digital clock and a clock face can show the same time in two ways.
adult: NC Y3 Measurement: tell and write the time from an analogue clock to the nearest minute; compare with digital. Builds on Y2 five-minute intervals (flagmins) and hours/half hours (flagclock).
Words: minute mark, minutes past, minutes to, digital, nearest minute. Common mistakes: reading only multiples of 5; swapping past and to; treating :09 as minutes to the hour.
In the lab your child counts seven marks to 3:07, sets 3:17 and 4:23, makes 5:42 as minutes to 6, matches 2:09, and spots the big-number-only mix-up.
